title: wordEncoding
summary: Create a word encoding object that maps words to indices and back.

gpu_support.notes: `wordEncoding` builds host text metadata and has no provider-resident numeric kernel.

description: `wordEncoding(documents)` creates a RunMat `wordEncoding` compatibility object from tokenized documents. `wordEncoding(words)` creates one from a word vector.
behaviors: `documents` must be a RunMat `tokenizedDocument` compatibility object.
`words` may be a string scalar, string array, character vector, character matrix, or cell array of scalar text. A character vector is treated as one word.
The returned object exposes `NumWords` and `Vocabulary`. `Vocabulary` is a 1-by-NumWords string array.
`Order` accepts `"first-seen"` and `"frequency"` for tokenizedDocument input. The default is first-seen order.
For frequency ordering, RunMat sorts by descending total count and uses first-seen order as a deterministic tie-breaker.
`MaxNumWords` accepts a positive integer or `Inf` for tokenizedDocument input. The option is applied after ordering.
RunMat rejects `Order` and `MaxNumWords` when the first input is a word vector, matching the documented MATLAB syntax.
First-class MATLAB object-array identity semantics are not required for this scalar model object and remain covered by the broader object infrastructure work.

examples.input:
documents = tokenizedDocument(["alpha beta alpha"; "gamma beta"]);
enc = wordEncoding(documents)

examples.output: `enc.Vocabulary` contains the two most frequent words.

faqs.question: Can the result be used with `doc2sequence`?
faqs.answer: Yes. `doc2sequence(enc, documents)` returns cell arrays of 1-by-S word-index vectors.

faqs.question: Does `wordEncoding` execute on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. It constructs host text metadata and does not use provider kernels.

example.input:
enc = wordEncoding(documents)
enc = wordEncoding(words)
enc = wordEncoding(documents, Name, Value)

points: `Order` must be `"first-seen"` or `"frequency"` and is only accepted for tokenizedDocument input.
`MaxNumWords` must be a positive integer or `Inf` and is only accepted for tokenizedDocument input.

gpu_residency: `wordEncoding` is host text/object metadata construction with no provider kernel.
